title: Australia news live: Catholic Schools NSW chief executive Dallas McInerney sacked after Icac appearance; Brethren church denies paying far-right activists
text: 21.21 EDT Catholic Schools NSW chief executive sacked after Icac appearance Penry Buckley The chief executive of Catholic Schools NSW, Dallas McInerney , has been sacked from his position following his appearance at the NSW Icac’s inquiry into allegations of corruption in the state’s Liberal party . In a statement shared today, the schools governing body said its board had “unanimously determined that there is a loss of confidence in Dallas McInerney’s ability to lead the organisation into the future”. As such, the Board has now terminated Mr McInerney’s employment agreement with Catholic Schools NSW. Interim CEO, Peter Yates, will remain in the role while a search process is conducted. The schools governing body has said it will not make any statement “regarding the inquiry or key witnesses” until Icac’s initial examination has been conducted, but says it will support an independent review of Catholic Schools NSW’s operations. title: California oil pipeline can continue to operate, judge rules
text: Sable’s Santa Ynez unit in Santa Barbara, in June. Photograph: Bloomberg/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Sable’s Santa Ynez unit in Santa Barbara, in June. Photograph: Bloomberg/Getty Images California California oil pipeline can continue to operate, judge rules State sought to stop system off coast of Santa Barbara from resuming operations after Trump ordered its reopening Dani Anguiano Thu 20 Aug 2026 20.13 EDT First published on Thu 20 Aug 2026 16.13 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google An oil pipeline can continue to operate off the California coast after a judge gave it the green light this week, despite the opposition of state regulators and environmental groups. The system off the coast of Santa Barbara resumed operations earlier this year for the first time in more than a decade after Donald Trump ordered Sable Offshore Corporation to reopen it, citing US energy needs during the war in Iran. It had been closed since 2015 when a burst pipe caused one of California’s worst oil spills, and its reopening was supposed to be governed by a federal consent decree.
